nodes.text: Let $N\geq 1$ and let $t(N)$ be the least integer $t$ such that there is no solution to\[1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}\]with $t=n_1<\cdots <n_k\leq N$. Estimate $t(N)$.

#294 : [ErGr80,p.35] number theory | unit fractions Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] could show\[t(N)\ll\frac{N}{\log N},\]but had no idea of the true value of $t(N)$. Solved by Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24] (up to $(\log\log N)^{O(1)}$), who proved that\[\frac{N}{(\log N)(\log\log N)^3(\log\log\log N)^{O(1)}}\ll t(N) \ll \frac{N}{\log N}.\] Proof expositions (0) If you would like to contribute an exposition of a proof related to this problem, please message a moderator or leave your exposition as a comment.
